findings.title: Cleanup uncertainty on a rejected raw acquisition is not adopted by the reader
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: The closure now correctly latches temporary cleanup failure, and delivered-handle failures now enter reader cleanupFailures. The remaining dependency boundary loses that state: acquireNativeFacts can reject after source closure.open/verification/read fails and its cleanup is uncertain; reader #adopt ignores the raw rejection for its own ledger, and #read only latches failures collected by its local cleanup. Because no sourceLease was delivered, workspaceLease.release can succeed and local failures stays empty, so a later read is admitted and reader.close can resolve despite upstream-owned uncertain FDs. A concrete proposed fault is a source open/unpack EIO plus failed source close using observeNativeFacts.closureOps; first rejection already owns cleanup_errors, then a new stable read on the same reader is not blocked. Also authority #streamDigest catch at313-314 replaces a retainFile error with changed(), losing the named syscall cause; authority:516 and reader:606 overwrite existing cleanup_errors when later cleanup also fails. Pure unpack assertions atT:1845/1849 prove the closure, not these outer boundaries; delivered cleanup test atT:835 proves a different path.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: Propagate source-acquisition cleanup uncertainty and all primary/cleanup causes into this reader’s existing private sticky ledger, including raw rejection after caller cancellation; merge rather than replace causes without retrying any numeric descriptor. Add one actual authority-to-reader fault assertion plus a canceled raw-rejection variant before accepting this requirement.

findings.title: No final closed/uncertain admission fence before resource delivery
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: After awaiting #readFacts the reader unconditionally sets delivered=true and returns resources. Final #readFacts checks source/workspace closures but never this.#closed or this.#cleanupUncertain; no guard runs after its last external callback or after the await before transfer. A supplied closureOps.close callback on a temporary directory release during final workspaceClosure.verify can synchronously call reader.close() and return normally. That closes admission, but the current verify still returns true and #read delivers facts; close merely waits for the admitted read then succeeds. Similarly an uncertain release of another already-delivered proof during final work need not refuse the in-flight proof. The start-binding reentry case only closes at binding.isCurrent before acquisition, and T:1454 intentionally closes after successful delivery; neither reaches this pre-transfer window. This is a static path, not an executed reentry test.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: After all callbacks/awaits and immediately before setting delivered, check the reader’s closed/uncertain state and reject into the existing all-attempt pre-delivery cleanup. Add a final-verification callback reentry case; preserve the existing rule that close after completed delivery does not destroy owner-held resources.

findings.title: Pinned film parser reopens a mutable path outside retained text limits
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: Authority streamDigest now obtains bounded retained text first, but nativeLineage subsequently invokes createPinnedOpenFilmUpstream.readProjectFilm(root). Its wrapper opens root/film.html again, only checks regular-file type, then handle.readFile() reads the whole current file into memory and copies it to a parser tmp folder. A film replaced or grown to a huge regular file after the bounded digest and before this later read is allocated before retained-text equality/final closure verification rejects it. The retained 8MiB/64MiB checks do not bound this second pathname read. F06 overwrites the file before acquisition, so the earlier bounded read rejects and the parser branch is never reached. Its onReadChunk counter counts closure text reads only; retainFile already streams the full file for hashing, so zero counted chunks does not mean zero physical I/O.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: Feed the existing approved pinned parser bounded, retained immutable film bytes in this authority path, with no artifact/pin or public DTO change; if an additional shared helper path is necessary, request MAIN’s exact scope. Add the original between-digest-and-parser growth/swap barrier case and describe the existing zero-counter assertion as bounded text decoding, not absence of all file reads.

findings.title: Blanket pageframe/film-poster refusal leaves normal R04 cache contract unfinished
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: The original arbitrary-key cache acceptance was removed, which fixes that permissive branch. The replacement refuses every pageframe triple and every film-poster.jpg, including legitimate native producer output; no stable round can ever accept them. Fixed upstream document GET warms the full-film poster, page media GET draws pageframes, and poster GET writes the same cache family. This is not a demand to implement public Studio integration: it is the original component contract to classify normal native-derived workspace items and allow a newly stable proved derivation. Contract explicitly permits unsupported when a particular instance cannot prove pairing, but MAIN also prohibits permanently unsupported normal necessary GET cache while declaring N1N2 complete. T:798 supplies arbitrary key/not-a-JPEG files and checks refusal only; it cannot prove a legitimate derivation is supported.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: Prove exact existing pinned producer/key/dependency pairing for the reachable normal cache families and test old-proof invalidation plus a fresh stable accepted round. If a specific family cannot be proven under current component capabilities, hand MAIN concrete producer/dependency evidence for an explicit bounded scope decision and keep that original R04 requirement UNPROVEN; do not restore broad whitelisting, derive expected duration from caches, or declare blanket refusal complete.

findings.title: Injected timeout/output tests do not prove raw-child fault lifetimes
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: T:947 drives production runner branches using a handwritten child object with pid4242; it is component transport injection, not an actual delayed/killed/reaped child. Hang kill manually emits close; stdout overflow manually emits5MiB; stderr emits nothing, so 256KiB stderr protection is untested. No injected-call hit counter is asserted: the real version query also receives250ms deadline; NATIVE_PROBE_TIMEOUT for the hang scenario can originate before the injected media child is created, and UNAVAILABLE can arise from version failure in the spawn scenario. Current real-child close case proves one ordinary probe child is still held at observed exit and gone after close; its read-rejected marker is appended after awaiting close, so that marker alone does not timestamp promise settlement. Actual timeout, abrupt exit, slow child/raw drain and stdout/stderr overflow with FD-close ordering remain explicit original requirements. Rotation/multistream real-tool normalizer assertions exist atT:976 but do not themselves use reader-held descriptors.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: Keep the labelled injected runner tests, assert the named transport branch actually fired, and add only the missing original real raw-child timeout/abrupt/output-limit and held-FD order cases under a future MAIN grant. Assert stderr as well as stdout limits; distinguish algorithm-only real-media normalization from retained-reader evidence and diagnostic media from A films.

findings.title: Original negative/fence matrix remains materially incomplete despite52 test titles
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: Positive/negative/directory/media dependency checks are now separate and static inspection supports the F02 correction. But its new success test uses absent markers: markers are supplied to Expected directly, not computeNativeEffectiveSidecars. Thus it can pass even if the originally broken style/transcript negative-lookup consumer branch is reintroduced. Translation test adds an uncommitted sidecar before reading and rejects classification, not translation consumption. Raw-caption test compares readdir order to retained names on this platform; if readdir is lexical (as in this fixture), sorting the result would still pass. New source-parent swap during acquisition is real FS but leaves video-moved as extra membership, so rejection does not isolate identity-check necessity. No awaited actual owner/base/control/generation or replaced-ref invalidation case reaches the new reader; brand tests call isLease/isNativeFactsLease rather than substitute a foreign capability into a real acquisition. Missing empty-directory birth alone and settings/style add/delete variants remain unasserted. These are explicit ticket:32 cases, not extra integration scope.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: Add narrowly targeted original missing cases with hit/barrier assertions and no alternate earlier refusal: style or heard-transcript absent consumer success+birth, empty-directory-only birth, current workspace generation/ref replacement and owner/commit/control liveness at a real await, and isolated parent/root identity swaps. Preserve raw caption order independently of video sorting; if platform order is naturally sorted, label that limit and obtain a discriminating consumer fixture rather than claim mutation coverage.

findings.title: Same-relative-path alias check is narrower than original physical isolation
findings.static_finding_or_coverage_gap: Source/workspace leaves are separate resource objects and same-path source-to-workspace hardlinks are correctly rejected. The only inode comparison is sourceRetained.get(the same relative path); regular-file checks contain no external-hardlink policy. A workspace leaf hardlinked to an identical external file has a different inode from committed source and passes this check, retaining an alias outside the safe tree. The original design explicitly refuses hardlink escape/aliases. Source and workspace empty directories also have membership identities, but enumeration closes temporary directory FDs and only file-parent/explicitly requested directories stay held; the actual component never asserts two-tree empty-directory retained ownership. The pure empty-directory case explicitly retains a directory in one closure and is not equivalent evidence.
findings.minimum_same_scope_action: Establish the original safe-root alias policy for external hardlinks (and cross-path aliases where relevant), and prove independent source/workspace resource allocations and empty-directory ownership with existing private closures. Do not equate two wrapper objects or matching bytes with physical isolation; no new public capability is needed.
